title: The 22 'unsolved' ADFGVX radio messages, Eastern Front, November 1918 (Childs corpus; Schmeh's list)

documents.shelfmark: James Rives Childs transcription, pages 73-217 (list provided by George Lasry on Schmeh's blog, 2017)

plaintext.source: Readings of 9 messages and parts of 3 in the comment thread under Schmeh's 2017 post (Norbert, Armin, Lasry and others); 10 never read.

transcription.source: Schmeh's blog page (msgs.txt), from the Childs transcription
transcription.notes: Count is the sum of the per-message letter counts in the NOTES table (22 messages, marked gaps excluded). msgs.txt mixes blog prose with the ciphertext, so --measure gives no clean figure. Mutilation in transmission (lost or added letters, marked gaps) is the obstacle.

system.summary: ADFGVX: 6x6 Polybius substitution to letter pairs followed by columnar transposition under a three-day key (lengths 16-19).
system.sibling_key: Fourteen published period keys (Lasry, Niebel, Kopal, Wacker) plus Lasry's sixteenth CHI key of 13 Nov 1918 from the 2017 thread, rebuilt here; used.
system.notes: Three published squares damaged by PDF dash collapse and repaired; transposition convention settled on page 100.

prior_solution.where: Published keys (Lasry et al.) and the 2017 comment thread under Schmeh's post (9 solved, 3 partial)

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.
tools: block-edit search with German quadgram model (blocks.py, lm_de.py)
key-free transposition annealer (keyless.py) with planted controls

solution.what: Made the fourteen published keys machine-readable; repaired three squares damaged by the PDF text layer.
Settled the transposition convention and reproduced page 100 by insertion search over all keys (score 140.7).
Read the 70 comments of the 2017 thread: 9 solved, 3 partial, 10 open; Lasry's sixteenth key found and its square rebuilt (24 of 36 cells).
Norbert's block-edit method reimplemented; re-derives 7 solved pages blind and finds the 22-24 Nov partial.
Two block edits against fifteen keys on the ten open messages; CHI key on the two page-153 messages.
Key-free attack on a planted 224-letter control does not recover the key; open messages (84-240 letters) are below reach.

Outcome split into parts per period key (one key per entry): six keys with their messages (9 solved, 3 partial) and the ten messages no known key fits (not solved), from the NOTES table; README one row per part.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): msgs.txt (Lasry's list of the 22 ciphertexts) as transcription; the readings table copied verbatim from NOTES.md to texts/residue22_decryption.md; keys.json (fifteen keys incl. the rebuilt CHI key) as key file. Ten messages have no reading.

Reading audit, per-document pass (George Lasry's sentence test): texts/residue22_decryption.md read message by message. The nine full readings build German sentences; the three partial readings have "..." gaps in most sentences and ten messages have no reading. The entry split into a read entry and a decoded, not read entry; class already solved -> read in part; fraction_read unknown -> 0.49 (letters).

Re-read (REREAD_BRIEF, b24): searched for readings of the residue messages published after 2017. Found a decipherment of a 27 Nov 1918 message of about 170 letters posted by 'prinz' on 17 Sept 2026 (reported by The Neuron, 18 Sept 2026, and news sites): keyword TRUPPENVERSCHIEBUNG, plaintext 'EIN ENGLISCHER KREUZER EINLIEG X SEWASTOPOL X S4STEN X EIN GESCHWADER DER X ALLIIERTEN FOLGT 26STEN X'. Childs p. 217 has 170 letters.

Known-plaintext check on p. 217 (b24_adfgvx_217.py): the transposition by TRUPPENVERSCHIEBUNG turns the 170 received letters into 85 pairs that map one to one onto the 85 plaintext letters (23 distinct pairs, 23 distinct letters, no conflict), and the recovered cells form a keyword-shaped square (T R U P E 4 / N . S C 2 H). Accepted; texts/p217_reading.md and _en.md. The same transposition and cells applied to the nine other open messages give noise.

VGADA (Childs p. 215): Norbert's two inserted groups with the Nov 22-24 key reproduce his raw decrypt exactly; aligned letter by letter with Baertl's 2017 corrected text (b24_adfgvx_vgada.py): 97 of 129 letters carried by both cells, 11 by one, 1 by none, 20 of Baertl's letters contradict the received cells and only 5 of those are one-cell errors ('S4N' twice where he reads '24N'; p. 217 has 'S4STEN' too). Partial reading kept (texts/vgada_partial_reading.md, 0.00 clean); stays decoded, not read.

VGADA residual search with the three length-22 keys and two free edits (gaps.py anneal, 6 restarts) before Norbert's edits were applied: noise (-7.4 per letter); his group insertions at the marked gap and after group 43 are what make it decrypt.

v3 verification: residue22 entry scored on its table file (0.188); the nine full readings extracted to texts/residue22_reading.md and rescored with v2_score.py: 0.87 explicit-hole (plain 0.565). Keeps read; reading field added.

outcome.method_basis: The fourteen period keys published by Lasry, Niebel, Kopal and Wacker for the Childs corpus, plus Lasry's sixteenth (CHI) key from the 2017 Cipherbrain comment thread, were applied with a block-edit search; the only full reading (page 100) had already been read in 2017.
outcome.notes: Nothing read here that the 2017 readers had not read; the thread consolidated and the sixteenth key rebuilt. Ten messages remain open, needing the Childs originals or an unlisted key. Split into outcome.parts per period key on 14 Oct 2026 (one key per entry, parts because the messages form one filed set): 9 solved, 3 partial, 10 open. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: the readings table split into two entries, the nine messages that read (state read) and the thirteen partial or open ones (decoded, not read); class already solved -> read in part, fraction_read 0.49 by letters. 23 Oct 2026 (b24): p. 217 read from the decipherment reported in Sept 2026 ('prinz', keyword TRUPPENVERSCHIEBUNG), verified here as known plaintext (85 pairs, one-to-one); VGADA's 2017 reading checked letter by letter (20 of Baertl's letters against the cells): stays partial.

parts.label: no known key fits
parts.basis: 0 solved, 0 partial, 9 open (p. 217 moved to its own part, 23 Oct 2026). None of the fifteen keys gives text with up to two block edits (best -6.7 nats per window against -4.4 to -6.0 for the solved pages); the CHI key fails on both p. 153 messages; a key-free attack fails its planted 224-letter control. Needs the Childs originals or an unlisted key.

texts.label: 22 ADFGVX messages, Childs pages 73-217 (Nov 1918): the nine read in full (pp. 100, 105, 109, 132, 146, 171, 176, 187 part 1 and its part 2 AFAFF)
texts.summary: German ADFGVX radio messages of November 1918 from James Rives Childs's transcription, listed as unsolved by George Lasry on Schmeh's blog in 2017. The readings, consolidated from the 2017 comment thread (Norbert, Armin, Baertl, Lasry), are routine traffic: march reports towards Belgrade, a repeat-telegram order, the Kertsch radio station, rouble rates after the break with the Soviet government; ten messages remain unread.

reading_review.note: v3 verification 23 Oct 2026: the sweep scored texts/residue22_decryption.md, the table of all 22 messages with the thirteen open/partial rows (explicit-hole 0.188), a false alarm. The nine messages read in full, extracted verbatim to texts/residue22_reading.md (X rendered as a stop), score 0.87 on the explicit-hole measure (20/23 sentences; plain 0.565, telegraphic abbreviations and numbers). Rests on the 2017 Cipherbrain readers' decryptions (Armin, Norbert, Lasry).

texts.label: the same file: three messages read only in part (p. 164 F-G-X, p. 164 VFGAG, VGADA p. 215) and nine with no reading (pp. 73, 152, 153 VFVAX and AXVAA, 158, 170, 176 GGDAA, 189, 198); p. 217 is now its own entry
texts.summary: Twelve of the 22 residue messages: three give fragments (Temesvar, Mirco; the Entente fleet at Kertsch with New Zealand, English and French divisions, VGADA, partial reading in texts/vgada_partial_reading.md); nine have no reading, because no known key fits them and several carry marked transmission gaps.
texts.note: Re-read 23 Oct 2026 (b24): p. 217 moved to its own entry (read, from the Sept 2026 decipherment, verified). Of the twelve left, VGADA p. 215 reproduces Norbert's 2017 decrypt with the Nov 22-24 key, but 20 of Baertl's 129 letters contradict the received cells, so its reading is part emendation (texts/vgada_partial_reading.md, 0.00 clean); the two p. 164 messages lose 44 letters each in transmission; the nine others fit no known key (incl. the p. 217 key). Blockers: needs-physical-access (the gaps; Childs's book pages) and no-key-material (the nine).

texts.label: Childs p. 217 (DXXXG GVXAX ..., 27 Nov 1918), one of the ten open messages
texts.summary: An English cruiser has put in at Sevastopol on the 24th; an Allied squadron follows on the 26th. Decipherment published by 'prinz' on 17 Sept 2026 (keyword TRUPPENVERSCHIEBUNG, a key Childs lists for later use), checked here against the figures: the 85 plaintext letters map one to one onto the 85 ADFGVX pairs (23 pairs, 23 letters, no conflict).

reading_review.note: Read 23 Oct 2026 (b24) from the decipherment reported in Sept 2026 ('prinz', The Neuron 18 Sept 2026), verified as known plaintext (b24_adfgvx_217.py): with transposition keyword TRUPPENVERSCHIEBUNG the 170 received letters give 85 pairs that map one to one onto the 85 letters (23 distinct each, no conflict), and the 23 cells fall into a keyword-shaped square (T R U P E 4 / N . S C 2 H). Every letter carried by its pair. Two telegraphic sentences; body 0.50 clean (1/2: 'einlieg', 'sewastopol' not in the word list), explicit holes 1.00. The same transposition and cells give noise on the nine other open messages.

gaps.item: nine open messages (pp. 73, 152, 153 x2, 158, 170, 176 GGDAA, 189, 198; 1,320 letters)
gaps.detail: no known key fits: the fourteen period keys, Lasry's CHI key, and (b24) the TRUPPENVERSCHIEBUNG transposition with the 23 cells recovered from p. 217 all give noise; key-free recovery is out of reach at 84-240 letters

gaps.item: three partly read messages (p. 164 F-G-X, p. 164 VFGAG, VGADA p. 215)
gaps.detail: transmission gaps (44, 44 and 11 marked letters; Norbert notes the transcript also lacks a whole line of p. 164); VGADA (b24): 97 of 129 letters carried by both cells, 20 of Baertl's 2017 letters contradict the received cells, so his text is part emendation; Childs's book pages would show whether the transcript dropped more

outcome.fraction_read_source: texts/residue22_decryption.md, letters per message (marked gaps excluded): the nine messages that read hold 1,945 of the 3,966 letters (0.490); the three partial (531 letters) and ten open (1,490) count as unread. The earlier "unknown" left the field unmeasured. 23 Oct 2026 (b24): p. 217 (170 letters) read from the Sept 2026 decipherment, verified as known plaintext; 2,115 of 3,966 letters (0.533) in messages that read.
